title: Spiral Traversal

statement.md: A risk report lays out a grid of instrument codes and wants them read in spiral order: start at the top-left, go right along the top row, down the right column, left along the bottom row, up the left column, then spiral inward until every cell is visited.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $m$ ($1 \le n, m \le 500$). Then $n$ lines of $m$ tokens, the grid, row by row.
outputFormat: All $n \times m$ tokens in spiral order on one line, space-separated.
constraints: tokens are alphanumeric, at most 10 chars

examples.explanation: Right along row 1, down column 4, left along row 3, up column 1, then right along row 2.

hints: Maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, right.
After each side, shrink the corresponding boundary and re-check the loop condition, single-row and single-column remnants are where bugs live.

editorial.md: The four-boundary method: keep `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` indices and loop while the region is non-empty. Each pass walks one full ring (four sides) and shrinks the boundaries inward. The two inner `if` checks (after walking right-then-down and left-then-up) prevent double-visiting when a single row or column remains.
The edge cases that break naive implementations are exactly the 1×m, n×1 and single-cell remnants, which is why the test set includes them explicitly.
